The cellar holds 14-16°C through the year; the corner near the boiler
drifts to 18°C and is the shelf for anything that wants speed.

Ferments want three different temperatures and this is the whole game:
vegetables at 18-22°C for the quick first phase, then cooler for
storage. Vinegar ferments like it warm — 25°C is not wasted on them.
Nothing wants the fridge except the finished kimchi and the quick
pickles.

Log: jars in the corner ferment visibly faster; jars by the outer wall
take twice as long and taste cleaner at the end. The wall wins for
flavour, the corner wins for impatience.
